summary: Specializing in Indology and computational fields, Jan Christian Schaffert studied at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026), where he also held a post with the EdiKILex project (attested 2026).
Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes, receiving his Magister der Philosophie (attested 2013).

Jan E. M. Houben works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Dutch Research Council (attested 1999) and Leiden University (attested 2000–2002), and became Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2003.

Jan Fontein specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin, served as curator at the Rijksmuseum (1955) and MFA Boston (1966–1992), and visited the Royal Ontario Museum (1990–1996).

Jan Gonda worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Leiden and Utrecht under Willem Caland and Anton Gerard van Hamel, later holding the Chair of Sanskrit (1929) and Indology (1932–1976) at Utrecht University.

Linguist and Indologist Jan Hanusz earned his PhD at Leipzig and completed his habilitation at Vienna under Georg Bühler and Friedrich Müller. He held a post at the University of Vienna from ~1885 to 1887.

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot specialized in Sinology and religious studies, studying at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz. He served as a professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).

Jan Jaworski worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Warsaw under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski, later serving as Privatdozent at the University of Warsaw in 1930.

Jan Jetso Boeles was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (1940–1945) under Nicolaas Johannes Krom and F. B. J. Kuiper, later serving as director of the Siam Society (~1959–1970).

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden, the Sorbonne under Chavannes and Cordier, and Berlin. He was a professor at Leiden University (1930–1954) and held visiting professorships at Columbia, Princeton, and Oxford.
Jan Kornelis de Cock was an Indologist. He completed his Ph.D. studies at the University of Amsterdam (~1894–1899) under the supervision of Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck.

Jan Laurens Andries Brandes specialized in Indology, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at Leiden University (Ph.D. 1884) and served as Keeper at the National Museum of Indonesia (~1884–1905).

Jan Michał Rozwadowski worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at Jagiellonian University and studied at Leipzig under Brugmann and Leskien, later serving as Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Jagiellonian University from 1904.

Working in history, archaeology, linguistics, and other fields, Jan Mrázek studied under doctoral supervisor Josef Zubatý. He later served as Associate Professor at the National University of Singapore (attested 2011).

Jan N. Bremmer specializes in religious studies and history/archaeology. After doctoral studies at VU Amsterdam and Amsterdam, he held posts at Utrecht University (1974–1990) and the University of Groningen (1990–2005), alongside fellowships at Harvard and the Getty.

Jan Nattier studied Buddhist studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Sinology at Indiana and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. She held professorships at Macalester College, Stanford, Indiana University Bloomington (1992–2005), and Soka University (2004–2010).

Linguist and Indologist Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay earned his PhD at Leipzig. He held professorships at Kazan (1874–1875), Tartu (1883–1893), Jagiellonian University (1893–1899), Saint Petersburg (1900–1914), and the University of Warsaw (1918–1929).

Jan P. Hogendijk specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning his doctorate at Utrecht University (1983), he taught at Frankfurt, Leiden (2004–2009), the University of Tehran, and Utrecht University as professor (2005–2020).

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann pursued Buddhist studies, completing his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper. He also studied under traditional teachers Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Rypka was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. After studying at the University of Vienna (~1905–1910), he held a faculty post at Charles University in Prague from ~1925 to 1958.
